name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: China's pause on rare-earth export controls expires 10 Nov with no renewal notice published
state: China's one-year suspension of its October 2025 rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and Beijing had published no notice renewing it, offering only case-by-case flexibility (Startup Fortune; Yahoo Finance). China's commerce ministry extended the wider US–China truce to 10 Jan 2027 on 28 Sep without naming the rare-earth suspension. China's rare-earth exports fell 9.6% year on year in January–September.
for_you: Rare-earth curbs tend to delay or raise costs for electronics, cars and wind turbines over months rather than days.
rubric_hit: Major export controls threatened between large economies = Watch

sources.title: Startup Fortune — China's rare earth truce runs out on November 10 with no renewal in sight
Yahoo Finance — China rare earth export pause nears expiry

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
